scenes.say: Ever get confused by JDK, JRE, and JVM? And what’s actually new in Java seventeen and twenty-one?
Here’s the stack: the JVM runs your compiled code. The JRE adds libraries so you can run apps. The JDK includes both, plus tools for building Java.

Recent Java long-term support releases added records for simple data, sealed classes to limit inheritance, pattern matching for easier type checks, text blocks for multi-line strings, and virtual threads for scalable concurrency.

scenes.question: Can you build Java apps with just the JRE?
scenes.right: No, you need the JDK for development tools like the compiler.
scenes.say: Watch out—if you only have the JRE, you can run Java apps, but you can’t build them. You need the JDK for development.
